plan.chapter_thesis: Electronic-photonic co-design represents the essential paradigm shift for scalable photonic computing, treating hardware geometry, electronic control, and algorithmic structure as a unified optimization problem rather than independent layers.
plan.reader_takeaway: Practical scalability in photonic computing requires adapting algorithms to physical constraints (analog precision, thermal crosstalk) and using physics-informed machine learning to automate the mapping of abstract functions to manufacturable device geometries.

argument_sequence.purpose: Establish the fundamental definition of co-design as a departure from drop-in replacement models, emphasizing the need for algorithmic adaptation to photonic constraints.
Introduce nanophotonic inverse design powered by deep learning as the primary mechanism for bridging algorithmic goals and physical geometries.
Explain how physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) and operators embed physical laws directly into the optimization loop to ensure realizability.
Address the critical constraint of fabrication tolerance and non-uniqueness, showing how co-design must account for manufacturing variations.
Detail specific architectural implementations like diffractive optical neural networks (DONNs) and physical neural networks (PNNs) that decouple algorithmic structure from hardware limits.
Analyze the role of electronic control overhead, specifically thermal crosstalk and phase variations, and the need for distributed calibration strategies.
Synthesize the role of advanced optimizers, including reinforcement learning and surrogate models, in automating the complex mapping between abstract functions and hardware.
Conclude with the system-level implication: heterogeneous integration and monolithic co-design are required to minimize latency and power overhead.

terminology_rows.note: Optimization of physical variables and geometrical parameters simultaneously to meet functional requirements using AI.
Neural networks that embed physical laws (PDEs) directly into the loss function to ensure physically realizable outputs.
Co-design paradigm where physical diffractive layers are jointly optimized with algorithmic functions.
Undesired optical interference in dense circuits caused by thermo-optic phase shifter heating.
Method to map input data to reduced feature vectors, mitigating computational burden of online training.

explanation_block_rows.title: The Co-Design Imperative: Beyond Drop-In Replacements
explanation_block_rows.goal: Define co-design as a unified optimization problem and establish why photonic substrates require specific algorithmic adaptations rather than acting as simple electronic substitutes.

explanation_block_rows.title: AI-Driven Inverse Design Mechanisms
explanation_block_rows.goal: Explain how deep learning and generative AI enable the simultaneous optimization of geometry and function, shifting from intuition-based to data-driven design.

explanation_block_rows.title: Embedding Physics via PINNs and Operators
explanation_block_rows.goal: Demonstrate how physics-informed architectures (PINNs, dynamic operators) reduce simulation latency and ensure adherence to physical laws during optimization.

explanation_block_rows.title: Robustness to Fabrication and Non-Uniqueness
explanation_block_rows.goal: Address the challenges of manufacturing variations and non-unique solutions, showing how co-design incorporates foundry constraints and reparameterization.

explanation_block_rows.title: Architectural Paradigms: DONNs and PNNs
explanation_block_rows.goal: Illustrate specific co-designed architectures where physical layers implement non-isomorphic functions, enabling compact on-chip learning without iterative feedback.

omitted_handle_reasons.C12_SCALABLE_PHOTONIC_NEURAL_NETWORKS_UT: Merged into Block 7 discussion of surrogate models to avoid redundancy with architectural focus here.

explanation_block_rows.title: Mitigating Electronic Control Overhead
explanation_block_rows.goal: Analyze thermal crosstalk and fabrication-induced phase noise as boundary conditions that necessitate distributed tuning and calibration strategies.

explanation_block_rows.title: Automation via Advanced Optimizers and Surrogates
explanation_block_rows.goal: Synthesize the role of reinforcement learning, meta-optimization, and surrogate scattering matrices in automating the mapping of abstract objectives to hardware.

explanation_block_rows.title: System-Level Integration and Future Trajectory
explanation_block_rows.goal: Conclude by linking co-design methodologies to heterogeneous integration platforms that reduce latency and power, defining the path toward scalable systems.
